To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

market participation in commercial agriculture, when it is limited to the supply of products to local retailers rather than wholesalers, has a positive and statistically significant impact on the in situ conservation effort of native chili varieties.
market commercialization of native chili varieties in the Amazon rain forest of Peru is positively associated with farmers’ participation in local retail markets.

farmers’ participation in commercial agriculture, specifically when they sell their products to retailers, is statistically significantly associated with a greater probability of cultivating native chili varieties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between market participation and agro-biodiversity loss.
the potential trade-off between market participation and agro-biodiversity conservation and the implications for policy design.
the relationship between market participation and agro-biodiversity loss.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
market participation is a key determinant of the in situ maintenance of native chili varieties in Ucayali.
the in situ conservation status of native chili varieties depends on a complex set of factors, including market participation, but that the latter does not necessarily imply agro-biodiversity loss.
the market participation of small farmers is not necessarily associated with the erosion of crop diversity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
farmers that sell chili to local markets are more likely to conserve native chili varieties than those farmers that only consume chili for self-use.
farmers who sell chili to local retailers are more likely to conserve native chili varieties.
the promotion of market participation of native chili varieties could help to achieve the goals of in situ conservation of crop genetic diversity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
market participation could be used as an effective tool for promoting the in-situ conservation of native chili crop varieties.
policies designed to promote the conservation of underutilised crop varieties could be implemented in such a way that they do not negatively impact crop biodiversity.
the in situ conservation policy should be based on the specific characteristics of the local market and the local farming system.
